title: `mode` returns every most frequent value
verdict: a list of all modes, in no stated order
description: `mode` returns all the values tied for most frequent, as several rows (a list per group); with `maintain_order=True` in order of first occurrence, otherwise in an unspecified order. NULL counts as a value (`[None, None, True].mode()` is `[None]`), on both engines. `mode().first()` picks one.
The docs are silent on the default order and on NULL counting as a value: a docs gap.
No upstream test pins the streaming engine's tie order; it may change between versions.
reference: `MODE` returns one value, any of the tie (`tie_pick`). A writer takes one element of Polars's list.

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_polars` runs each expression on edge cases (0, ±1, ±2, 3, ±7, the bounds of the integer width; 0.5, ±2.5, 7, 1e308, ±inf, NaN; NULL), one row at a time, and compares each row with Lean's outcome of the Substrait call under each candidate option (`substrait-check --outcomes`). Observations are Polars programs whose result is recorded as it is. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), Rust crates at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3), on macOS arm64.

notes: Streaming gives what in memory gives on every probe and observation cited here.
The observations' frames hold a few rows, which streaming runs as one-row morsels; the probes' 6000-row columns cover morsels of many rows.

`python -m sverify_dev.probe_polars --diff --write` runs each probe one row at a time and on a 6000-row column with `collect(engine='in-memory')` and `collect(engine='streaming')`, and each observation twice: its `df(...)` frame's `select`, `with_columns`, `filter`, `sort`, `unique`, `join` and `group_by` go through the streaming engine the second time (`StreamingFrame`); the `s-` observations collect a lazy query on each engine themselves. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), macOS arm64.

evidence.note: in memory: group_tuples(parallel, maintain_order), keep every group of maximal size in group order; NULL is a group
streaming ungrouped: group_by(value).agg(len), filter(count == max(count)); tie order from the streaming group_by unless maintain_order
may return several values; maintain_order parameter; silent on the default order and on NULL counting as a value

provenance.notes: Corrected the description: it said the order of the modes is not documented; the docs offer `maintain_order` and are silent on the default. Added NULL counting as a value.
